approach: Read the acceleration in each of the three time segments, find the velocity at each segment boundary, and add the distance covered in each segment.

steps.text: From t = 0 to 4 s, acceleration is 2 ms⁻² from rest. Find the velocity and distance covered by the end of this segment.
From t = 4 to 8 s, acceleration is 0, so the lift moves at the constant velocity 8 ms⁻¹. Find the distance covered.
From t = 8 to 12 s, acceleration is −2 ms⁻². Check that the lift comes to rest exactly at t = 12 s.
Find the distance covered while the velocity falls from 8 ms⁻¹ to 0 over this last segment.
Add the three distances to get the total height above the starting point.

common_mistakes.text: Treating zero acceleration in the middle segment as zero velocity, so skipping the 32 m travelled at constant speed and adding only the first and last segments: 16 + 16 = 32 m.
